title: Monotonicity of function-computation bounds
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine, let $f$ be a function, and let the input and output encodings into words over the machine's alphabet be injective. If $M$ computes $f$ within input-indexed time and space bounds $t,s$, and $t(a)\le t'(a)$ and $s(a)\le s'(a)$ for every input $a$, then $M$ computes $f$ within bounds $t',s'$ using the same encodings.
hypotheses_covered: The input and output encodings into words over the alphabet are injective
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine that computes a function $f$ between
given injective encodings within input-indexed time bound $t$ and space bound
$s$, and let $t'$ and $s'$ be bounds with $t(a) \le t'(a)$ and
$s(a) \le s'(a)$ for every input $a$.  Then $M$ also computes $f$ between the
same encodings within the bounds $t'$ and $s'$.
